fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Unam Sanctam and the captured spiritual realm", "body": "Gabe roots the whole conversation in the Hermetic maxim as above, so below, and in the papal bull Unam Sanctam, which he reads as declaring the spiritual realm preeminent over the material and handing the Vatican a claim over all things spiritual. His example is light: defined as both particle and wave, yet in his view science must still explain it in materialist terms, which he calls regulatory capture of the spirit. Chance adds that papal authority rests on belief in a literal historical Jesus, while Gabe senses that old paradigm now collapsing, visible in the germ versus terrain debate."}, {"title": "What public and private mean in law", "body": "Asked to define the two spheres, the conversation casts the public as regulated, a place where standing and sovereignty are diminished, and the private as so loosely defined that it becomes an anything goes space for anyone seeking to live without rulers. Gabe describes handing an ID through a car window as giving joinder, and argues the key to staying private is to remain unknown and never do an officer's job for them. Chance wonders whether accepting gifts and services pulls people into the public, then uses Spider-Man: No Way Home, where one friend demands a lawyer and the other talks freely, as a parable."}, {"title": "Stars, towers and the analemma as pillars", "body": "Gabe maps the two pillars onto the sky: Polaris, visible most of the year, as the public and masculine, and Sigma Octantis, hidden below the horizon for much of it, as the private and feminine. In his three part video series he ties the South Tower of 9/11 to the private star and the North Tower to Polaris, reading their order of collapse as Unam Sanctam inverted and driven into the earth. He then traces the analemma, whose crossing points he places at tax day on April 15 and near Vulcanalia, a festival he links to Pompeii, Etna and Krakatoa, while Chance connects both dates to coins and blacksmiths."}, {"title": "Language, names and debt", "body": "Gabe calls English angelese, a duplicitous tongue whose everyday words carry different meanings once Black's Law Dictionary defines them as terms of art, and treats the Bible as public notice, a program written before, on which he says law is founded. He offers that the bank is the bench a judge sits on and that sin stands for standing in negative, meaning debt. Chance adds sin as synthetic, contrasting a full legal name, which he says lets the system identify people, with a Christian name and with nature, where a deer is simply self existing. They trade tactics like answering that your name is private."}, {"title": "Standing, preparation and nobody in charge", "body": "Stressing that this is philosophy, not legal advice, Chance asks whether people need to correct their standing on paper. Gabe favors dozens of lines of defense, starting with conversation that is cordial but difficult, conditional acceptance, and a declaration of status filed with the county clerk in advance, plus knowing the local sheriff. He reads FDR's proclamations 2039 and 2040 as casting civilians as belligerents, and says being organized is the answer. Chance argues nobody is truly in charge, likening the system to a game of Monopoly whose masters do not know all their own rules, while Gabe sees an overwhelming Aquarian deluge of truth anyone can master."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: InnerVerse is back in 2022 with the return of the ever-reliable Slick Dissident, AKA Gabriel, for a conversation about living in two worlds. What is the difference between the public and private spheres? How has this dichotomy been used against the people? And what can we do to correct our standing so that we stay in sovereignty? These are the questions on the table for today's episode.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Paperwork, presumption and careful first steps", "body": "Chance Garton opens the members' hour by asking how people correct their status, stressing that nothing here is legal advice. Slick Dissident urges caution first, saying the best teacher is other people's failed attempts. He describes affidavits as sworn statements that must be true, and floats beginner ideas from his own research, such as declaring that one's weapons are arms rather than firearms, or stating that one is not a party. Chance adds his reading of enfranchisement as a kind of incorporation. Both frame these as theories they are studying, not proven remedies, and Gabe stresses that the burden of objecting falls on the individual."}, {"title": "Private members' associations and keeping exchanges private", "body": "Chance Garton raises private members' associations as an area for further research, pointing to homeowners associations and elite clubs as examples of how much latitude private membership can grant. He describes his own sound healing as a gift offered in exchange for a gift. Slick Dissident suggests that fraternal orders were the original private associations and notes that several local lodges have closed. He argues that keeping terms open protects privacy, and offers his view that many legal troubles begin when people negotiate in public, comparing it to a traffic stop where the car is treated as private space."}, {"title": "Myth as the script behind public events", "body": "Both hosts read current events as staged mythology. Chance Garton suggests the public is being handed open evidence of corruption so that institutions can be scapegoated and replaced with something more centralized, a view he offers as his own interpretation. Slick Dissident links police and lawyers to the sacrificial goat of Yom Kippur, and casts Trump as Saturn and Biden as Jupiter in a ritual timed to the great conjunction. He then retells Ovid's three books on love, its errors and its remedy as a model for how a writer may ride, and hasten, an empire's decline."}, {"title": "When the private is dragged into public view", "body": "Slick Dissident works through a list of news items he reads as rituals that expose the private, from a president's medical details and announced cyber attacks to drive through testing, airport scanning and NASA probes carrying human information. He argues that powerful players privatize the benefits of a deal while the public absorbs the liabilities. Chance Garton brings up liminal spaces, and Gabe ties them to Mercury, the god of thresholds and thieves. The pair also revisit the September 11 attacks through Gabe's symbolic readings of Building 7, Solomon Brothers and an anagram he finds in In God We Trust."}, {"title": "Living in both worlds from the inside out", "body": "Chance Garton argues that natural rights can only be described in the negative, as everything except what one has no right to do, while legal systems run on definitions that create jurisdiction. He doubts that Babylon is going anywhere and suggests people will always live in both worlds, so the real work is honoring the divine source within and letting that inner order shape the outer one. Slick Dissident answers with a reading of Moses' broken tablets as the birth of the spoken, living law, and urges listeners to make a steady habit of objecting to presumption."}]

fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "A mask is a perfect screen for other people to project their insecurities onto.", "author": "Gabe (Slick Dissident)", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/794d3a0b-c42b-4791-84c3-f79eff430f4c/SLICK-DISSIDENT.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "People are much more afraid of what I think the truth is, which is that actually nobody's in charge.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "I do believe that we're coming to a time where there is a collapsing of that paradigm, and we are almost being given permission to come to things with a new approach.", "author": "Gabe (Slick Dissident)", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/794d3a0b-c42b-4791-84c3-f79eff430f4c/SLICK-DISSIDENT.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "The investigation of law is a very spiritual matter whenever you go beyond just the mundane aspects of it and look at these dualities as representatives of your own inner pillars.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "The key to staying private is to remain unknown. If an officer or public servant doesn't have your name on a piece of paper already in advance, then there's no reason for you to even work with them.", "author": "Gabe (Slick Dissident)", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/794d3a0b-c42b-4791-84c3-f79eff430f4c/SLICK-DISSIDENT.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "In nature, a deer is not named Jeff. To stand in the negative is to be in debt, and if you're in debt, then you are not calling the shots.", "author": "Gabe (Slick Dissident)", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/794d3a0b-c42b-4791-84c3-f79eff430f4c/SLICK-DISSIDENT.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "The truth is overwhelming, but it's there to have and it's there for us to master, and you don't gotta pay some school to access it anymore.", "author": "Gabe (Slick Dissident)", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/794d3a0b-c42b-4791-84c3-f79eff430f4c/SLICK-DISSIDENT.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}]
